Subject: Order Form + MSA: IP and training language (redlines attached)

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — BrightData is excited about Redwood's latency profile and the Dedicated option. Our legal team attached proposed redlines for the MSA and Order Form. The main open points are:

- Output ownership: we require a clear assignment that BrightData owns customer-facing output and retains title for downstream productization.
- Training / model use: we want an explicit opt-out from model training and downstream model use unless we provide written consent.
- Feedback license: our standard asks for a narrow telemetry/bug-fix license (no broad rights to use Customer Content for model improvement).

Attached: BrightData_Proposed_Redlines.docx (redline + comment bubbles).

Can you confirm who on Redwood legal will review and whether there are guided concessions (e.g., telemetry allowed if aggregated/anonymized)? Also please share any commercial uplift if training opt-out is accepted.

We'd like to keep the procurement timeline tight — aiming to sign the order form the week of July 24 if possible.

Thanks,

Laura/Ben — forwarding BrightData's redlines. High level: they want strong output assignment + full training opt-out unless they opt in, and a narrow feedback license. This is a classic procurement ask that affects our product and revenue model. Quick thoughts:

1) Output ownership: we can accept that BrightData has title to their proprietary customer-facing output, but we should preserve limited rights for Redwood to use output for debugging, billing, and aggregated analytics. Suggest language: "Customer retains title to Customer Output; Redwood retains the right to use aggregated/non-identifiable metadata and logs for monitoring, billing, and product improvement subject to anonymization and internal access controls."

2) Training opt-out: we should offer a formal training opt-out for an additional fee (one-time or recurring uplift) and include a mechanism in the Order Form to enable/disable. Outright unconditional no-training will materially reduce our ability to improve models; we need commercial protection.

3) Feedback license: propose a narrow license limited to "bug fixes, service improvements, and safety research" and explicitly exclude redistribution or model retraining on raw Customer Content.

Action items: Laura, can Legal review and propose counterlanguage and a suggested uplift? Ben, can you estimate the support/ops cost delta if training opt-out is enabled for a Dedicated pool (rough order of magnitude)? I drafted a response (attached) — use that as starting point.

Jordan
Director, Sales — Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.com]

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: jordan.blake@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: legal-ops@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 12 Jul 2028 11:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Order Form + MSA: IP and training language (redlines attached)

Jordan — reviewed BrightData's redlines. Summary and proposed positions below (high-level + suggested clause text). I didn't redline the entire doc here; I've attached a formal redline with tracked changes.

Summary of risk: BrightData's draft assigns broad "Output" ownership and proposes a near-total prohibition on any model improvement from Customer Content. That is commercially aggressive. We can compromise but must: preserve our ability to run aggregated telemetry, retain an escape for critical safety improvements, and carve out billing/ops uses.

Proposed positions (short):
- Output: Customer retains title to Customer Output. Add explicit carveouts: (i) Redwood internal logs and aggregated metrics remain usable for monitoring/billing; (ii) Redwood may retain a copy for dispute resolution/forensics under confidentiality safeguards.

- Training: Offer an Order Form checkbox: "Training Opt-Out: Customer elects that Redwood shall not use Customer Content or Customer Output to train or improve Redwood models." If checked, add a Commercial Uplift clause: "Customer agrees to an X% uplift on per-token charges or a fixed surcharge to offset lost model improvement economics." Provide suggested uplift range of 15–30% depending on scope (hosted vs dedicated).

- Feedback license: Narrow, time-limited, and purpose-limited license. Suggested text: "Customer grants Redwood a non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free license to use de-identified, aggregated feedback data solely to diagnose, fix, and improve Redwood's services, excluding use to train foundational or customer-facing language models without separate written consent."

Suggested clause snippets (can be copy/paste into the counter):
"Customer Output; Title. Customer retains title to Customer Output produced by the Service. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood may use (a) aggregated and anonymized metrics and telemetry; and (b) Customer Data necessary for billing, security investigations, and to comply with law, subject to confidentiality obligations."

"Training Opt-Out. The Order Form may include an explicit box to opt out of Redwood using Customer Content or Customer Output for training. If Customer elects Opt-Out, the Parties agree on a commercially reasonable surcharge, set forth in the Order Form. Opt-Out shall not prevent Redwood from using aggregated and de-identified telemetry that cannot be traced to Customer or individual end users."

I've attached a redline file with language and callouts. If we accept an opt-out, we should have a clear commercial uplift number and an operational mechanism (flag on the customer account, audit logs, and compliance attestations).

Next steps: Jordan — confirm whether you want me to send the counter with the uplift ranges included or keep commercial specifics for the finance/sales lead. Ben — please give an ops-support estimate by end of day. I'll prepare the formal counter to BrightData once we have Ben's number.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: RBW_Response_Redlines.docx (docx)]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Hi Maria — thanks for sending the redline. We've reviewed internally and can propose a compromise that keeps us both safe and on a clear commercial path. Main points in our counter:

- Output ownership: Redwood accepts that BrightData retains title to Customer Output. We will add explicit carveouts allowing Redwood to use aggregated/anonymized telemetry, logs for billing/security, and copies of data for dispute resolution under confidentiality protections (see attached counterredline).

- Training opt-out: We can offer a training opt-out as an Order Form selectable option. If BrightData elects opt-out, there will be a commercial uplift. To be transparent, our initial suggested uplift range is 20% on per-token usage (or a negotiated fixed surcharge for Dedicated capacity). This is flexible; happy to discuss specifics on the call.

- Feedback license: We propose a narrow, time-limited license allowing Redwood to use de-identified/aggregated feedback for debugging and product stability. Any use for model retraining will require separate written consent.

Attached is our counterredline (Redwood_Counterredlines.pdf) and a one-page summary of the Opt-Out flow. Please review and let us know a few slots for a short call next week — I can do Monday 10–11am PT or Tuesday 2–4pm PT. If you prefer, we can send the counter via DocuSign for expedited review: https://app.docusign.com/prepare/abcdef1234567890

If BrightData decides an immediate no-training box is non-negotiable, please let us know so we can provide a firm uplift quote and operational plan.

Best,
